correctness.rationale: The boundary specialization is algebraically exact. In the overshoot regime, the normalized max statistic follows \(F_p(q)=q/(q-1)^{2p}\). The inequality \(F_p(q)>2\) for all \(q>2\) is exact iff the proof condition \(p\le1/4\) applies, and for \(p>1/4\), \(F_p'(2)=1-4p<0\) forces finite crossing. The post-crossing recurrence is exactly linear.

value.rationale: Padam's defining novelty is its partial-adaptivity exponent. The exact scalar theorem shows that this exponent controls a qualitative transition between persistent oscillation and finite self-stabilization under the same historical-max mechanism. The critical value \(p=1/4\) is mathematically sharp and lies in a range already prominent in Padam's theory, making the result a meaningful diagnostic rather than an arbitrary slice.
